title: RAW UNREVIEWED: reapplying a stored relation pattern must rebind arguments unlike reusing its earlier result
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A compiling author may abbreviate a previously stated relation or instruction and apply it to a new item, rather than refer to the original item or result. Compare exactly two whole-passage accounts: reuse an earlier result token unchanged, or reuse an earlier relation pattern with one explicitly written new argument. The later dependent expression must then have different antecedents. Renaming the domain cannot erase that dependency difference. No Voynich word is assigned a meaning here.

design.mechanism: Textual compression by parameterized reuse versus token reference. Historical similiter hic from GDT1032 motivates relational reuse qualitatively, not a proven argument-rebinding construction.
design.unit: Complete already preserved GDT1153 paragraphs with all literal groups and uncertainty retained; choose the smallest complete candidate with an explicit earlier two-role construction, a later distinct written operand and a further written dependent consumer under one prospectively specified grammar. Candidate selection is a declared exploratory authoring task, not a claimed existing match.
design.contrast: TOKEN: R(a,b) yields a referent r and later reuse returns r with original arguments. PATTERN: store lambda x.R(a,x), later reuse with c yields R(a,c) and a new referent. Both retain the same surface inventory, composition grammar and fixed valencies.
design.prediction: The subsequent consumer must retain b or r under TOKEN but c or the newly instantiated relation under PATTERN. Deleting or changing the explicit c expression must change a downstream written dependency only in PATTERN. Require the consequence through the entire paragraph, not merely a stored diagnostic object.
design.scope: RAW shortlist for exploratory whole-passage authoring, not execution-ready. Available inputs: GDT1153 WHOLE_CONTEXTS.md and CASES.json; GDT1032 REPORT.md; GDT1138 REPORT.md and its failed producer/consumer traces. Concrete next task: author two complete dependency analyses of one already owned paragraph with every unassigned position visible; reject if no actual distinct operand and downstream written consumer can be specified. A confirmed lexeme is not required to attempt this, but any proposed lexical value first needs words profile and claim-bearing evidence. Preserve GDT1153 strict prior-choice failure, GDT1140 incomplete status reading, GDT616 failure, GDT1138 missing producers/consumers and IL025 dynamic-recipe control failure. Do not use legacy semantic card meanings or call stored references a completed reading. No subsequent consumer means no tested distinction; no posthoc per-form repair. IDEA768 typed role-transform applications in the old music account is a related predecessor, not new evidence; this proposal retains no music lexicon and contrasts result-token identity with parameterized pattern reuse through a later written consumer.
